Svartifoss turns your watch into a remote for the music playing on your phone. Here\'s everything you can do from your wrist.

The watch screen is split into four zones — top, bottom, left and right. Tapping a zone runs the action you assigned to it. By default the left zone plays or pauses, the right skips to the next track, and the top and bottom change the volume.

Double-tap the centre of the now-playing screen to open a panel of four slots — three round buttons and one wide row beneath them. Left alone, the slots mirror the buttons the playing app puts in its own notification, so you get its real like, shuffle and repeat controls. Assign any action to a slot, or set it to \"None\" to hide it, under Actions on the phone.

The four edge zones each support separate single, double and long-press actions. The center\'s single tap is also configurable; its double-tap always opens Quick actions, while its long-press opens the face picker, queue, or nothing according to Settings → Behavior.
If your watch has side buttons, you can assign single, double and long-press actions to them too. They keep working even when the screen is off.

Choose whether the rotating crown or bezel changes volume, seeks through the track, or does nothing under Settings → Behavior → Rotary crown / bezel. On watches that expose crown turns as buttons, assign them in Controls instead.

Swipe up, down or left on the now-playing screen can each be configured to open anything — the actions menu, the playback queue, skip tracks, your playlists, and more. Configure each one in Controls, choosing Music playing or No playback. By default, swiping up opens the actions menu and the others do nothing until you assign them. Swipe right is left alone — that\'s the universal Wear OS gesture to exit the app.

Save a link to a track, album, mix or playlist from Spotify, YouTube Music, Apple Music, TIDAL, Deezer, Amazon Music or SoundCloud, then assign it to any button, gesture or panel slot. The quickest way in is to share the link straight to Svartifoss from the streaming app; you can also paste a copied link or type one in. No account or login is needed — the watch asks the phone to start playback, so a shortcut plays instead of just opening the app.

Assign \"Play liked songs\", \"Play liked songs, shuffled\" or \"My playlists\" to any button, gesture or swipe to jump straight into your music without touching the phone. \"Search history\" remembers your recent searches on the watch — press and hold one to delete it.
Swipe from the left edge to leave the player. It can pause playback automatically when you exit — enable it in Settings.

The current track also shows up in your watch\'s own media controls and recent apps, so you can control playback from there as well.

Svartifoss started as a personal project — I wanted to bring Music Center for Wear up to date with what\'s possible today, just so I could use it myself every day. It turned out well enough that I decided to share it with everyone. This is my first app, and there\'s nothing quite like seeing something you built turn out to be useful to other people too.

Svartifoss lets you control music on your phone from your Wear OS watch — with a fully customizable remote tailored to your device.

Svartifoss means “Black Falls” in Icelandic — named after the waterfall in Vatnajökull National Park, where dark basalt columns frame a narrow cascade. Like water over stone, music flows through the app.
Watch settings are configured here on the phone and synced automatically to your paired watch.
Svartifoss is free and open source - buy me a coffee if it\'s useful to you :D
